overall_take: Beth's branch tree and Brennan's non-tonal son fork are the proof that Disco-grade writing is achievable in this engine — those scenes pass the 'I'd play this without the clinical scaffolding' test. Everything else is the gap. If one thing changes before the next playtest, it's that rapport — the system you spent M34/M38/M58 building — must stop being a one-shot per case. Right now most cases have a single branched moment with rapport_delta authored at it; the other 6–9 history items are flat exposition, and 'pulling away' (rapport ≤ −2) is a banner state that almost never triggers because there aren't enough dismissive branches to get there. The Disco bar isn't the *quality* of any one line, it's the *density* of consequential choices. Until rapport is a continuous variable the player feels they're holding through the encounter, every case is a tutorial wearing Beth's dress.

findings.title: Disco-density failure: 1.4 branched beats per case is a one-off, not a system
findings.file_or_case: all content/cases/*.yaml (cross-cutting; Patel, Brennan, Beth carry the catalogue)
findings.body: Across 17 cases there are 24 branch_choices blocks and 7 min_rapport disclosures. Eleven of seventeen cases have exactly ONE branched beat; six have two; none have three. The rapport gauge (KernelState.rapport clamped −3..+3, surfaced on screen as 'warming up / engaging / guarded / pulling away') therefore moves between roughly +2 and 0 in normal play and the 'pulled away' patient-silenced banner at lines 3364-3370 of EncounterScreen is functionally unreachable without deliberate trolling. Disco's bar is not the quality of one Tom-in-the-relatives'-room line — it's that every dialogue node carries texture, cost, or refusal. Right now the player learns the trick of 'pick the compassionate option' once and never feels the gauge as a held variable. Underlying cause: branches were authored as set-piece moments, not as the default shape of dialogue.
findings.recommendation: Set a per-case floor of 4 branched history beats and 2 min_rapport disclosures, and add 'silencing branches' (rapport_delta −2) to at least one early history item in every case so the 'pulling away' banner is a real failure mode a tired player can reach. The Beth hen-do and Brennan SDH cases are the templates — don't add tests, port their density.
findings.evidence: Beth (case_anaphylaxis_adult_peanut.yaml L5252–5358 for the layered Dom/Tom branches), Brennan (case_head_injury_doac_brennan.yaml L9166–9234 for the trilemma + min_rapport disclosure), vs Sarah (case_ectopic_minors_sarah.yaml: only hx_pregnancy is branched), Williams, Okafor, Marcus, Kowalski, Priya, Okonkwo, Ahmed, Oduya (1 branch each). EncounterScreen.tsx L3331 ('rapportCollapsed = cs.rapport <= -2') reads a state that the content can barely produce.

findings.title: Recurring NPCs were drafted then abandoned at the shift seam
findings.body: In Beth's case the paramedic Dom is named, given a shift-since-06:30 voice, and EXPLICITLY tells the player 'the friend Sarah came with us, she had belly pain, I think she's pregnant' (L5266–5270). That is the arc reveal handed to you in dialogue. Then Sarah's case (8376–) never names Dom; the hen-do arc unlock is mechanical (hx_friend_in_resus, hx_pain_started_earlier) and the paramedic source is absent entirely from her history items. Anya the triage nurse has an identical fate in Patel's case (named, given a second-day-on-triage backstory, then never reappears). HANDOVER §Story already flags this; it's listed as a TODO but it's the single highest-leverage rewrite in the catalogue because the arc reveal is already there — only the *who tells you* is missing. Underlying cause: arcs were authored as kernel mechanisms (unlocks_history_id) rather than as repeating-character beats.
findings.recommendation: Add one Dom-sourced history item to Sarah ('the paramedic Dom comes through to your bay — he wanted to tell you what he saw before he left'), gated by the arc reveal, with the same minute-by-minute texture as Beth's L5256. Same surgery on Anya across cases that share her overnight. This is ~6 history items of authoring and lifts the catalogue from 'linked cases' to 'an ED with regulars'.
findings.evidence: case_anaphylaxis_adult_peanut.yaml L5251 (Dom introduced), L5266–5270 (Dom flags Sarah's pregnancy), vs case_ectopic_minors_sarah.yaml L8462+ (no paramedic source at all); case_chest_pain_patel_ambient.yaml L7321–7351 (Anya the second-day triage nurse); HANDOVER.md §5 Story TODO.

findings.title: EncounterScreen is a 1331-line co-located junk drawer that has stopped paying its split tax
findings.body: The M61 split moved phase bodies into ./phases/ but left fifteen distinct components in one file: EncounterScreen, EncounterHeader, VignetteCard, SectionTabs, DeteriorationTimers, ShiftLog, HistoryPhase, ConsultantInterruptModal, PatientDeathModal, ConsultantWalkIn, ConsultantInterruptEmote, HistoryNpcSprite, BranchPicker, DifferentialPhase, DebriefPhase, CitationLine, plus collectClues / pickCardClass / statusLabel / firstName / gatedHistoryIds / visibleHistoryItems / isHistorySilenced / rapportLabel helpers. Three of these (ConsultantWalkIn, ConsultantInterruptEmote, ConsultantInterruptModal) own their own intervals, walk-cycle state, and SVG dangerouslySetInnerHTML; they have nothing to do with the encounter section pipeline. The DebriefPhase computes a ScoreReport via scoreCase from state/sim and does its own templating of pearls/pitfalls/sources — it is a whole screen in disguise. The clue board's selectedClues lives as local useState (L3801) which means tabbing away from Differential and back loses every clue the player selected — a silent gameplay bug born of the file's size. Underlying cause: the file is the project's default destination for any 'beat that fires inside an encounter', and nothing has been pulled out since.
findings.recommendation: Carve three modules: ./encounter/consultant/{Modal,WalkIn,Emote}.tsx (the McGrath beats are a coherent subsystem), ./encounter/DebriefScreen.tsx (move scoreCase orchestration with it; DebriefPhase should be a screen, not a phase), and ./encounter/dialogue/{HistoryPhase,BranchPicker,HistoryNpcSprite,rapport}.tsx. While you're in there, lift selectedClues into the kernel as cs.selectedClueIds so cross-tab persistence isn't broken.
findings.evidence: src/ui/encounter/EncounterScreen.tsx L2768–4099 (top-of-file imports through CitationLine); 15 components confirmed by function-header scan; DifferentialPhase local-state bug at L3801 (`const [selectedClues, setSelectedClues] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set())`).

findings.title: Kernel boundary is porous in exactly the place where determinism matters
findings.body: The kernel exposes getState() that returns a *mutable reference* to KernelState including Maps and Sets (L1564). EncounterScreen.tsx calls it on every render (L2846–2847) and HistoryPhase calls it again inside its body (L3316) instead of receiving ks as a prop. Because the kernel mutates Sets/Maps in place during advance() and toggleAction(), the UI is doing reference-equal comparisons against an object it watches mutate — which is why useSim((s) => s.tick) at L2844 exists as a force-refresh shim. The system works because tick is bumped on every notify, but it means the kernel is no longer the deterministic island the original prompt asked for ('deterministic event scheduler / tick loop … React/Phaser are just views onto it'). The risk is not today; it is that the next person who adds a feature will reach across the boundary and the snapshot tests will pass while the runtime view diverges. Underlying cause: the kernel was designed read-only-by-convention rather than read-only-by-shape.
findings.recommendation: Either freeze the snapshot returned by getState() (Object.freeze on entry + Readonly types end-to-end), or expose narrowed selectors (getCaseRuntime(caseId): Readonly<...>, getDeteriorationTimers(caseId): readonly DeteriorationTimer[]) and forbid raw getState() outside tests. The Zustand subscribe-by-tick shim becomes unnecessary the moment selectors return value-equal data.
findings.evidence: src/sim/kernel.ts L1563–1565 (getState returns this.state directly), L2073–2075 (notify mutates in place); src/ui/encounter/EncounterScreen.tsx L2844 (`useSim((s) => s.tick)`), L2846–2847, L3316 (two separate getState calls in one render tree).

findings.title: Citation density is bimodal — the paeds and obstetric cases are the SAQ-vulnerable ones
findings.body: Across cases citation counts vary from 4 (Amir paeds DKA) to 18 (Kowalski variceal UGIB). The four lightest-cited are the paediatric DKA, paeds anaphylaxis, ectopic, and adult DKA — exactly the cohort an FRCEM examiner can drown a candidate in (BSPED 2021 rev 2024 has discrete dose-bands, JBDS-IP 2023 has bedside numbers, RCOG GTG 21 has explicit serum βhCG cutoffs and the 2023 discriminatory-zone deprecation). The Amir case has only one BSPED citation; the corrected-Na formula and the 0.5–1% cerebral oedema mortality figure are stated bare. The Sarah case mentions GTG 21 once but doesn't cite the 2023 NG126 update directly. Underlying cause: cases were authored when their topic was the focus and got citation passes proportional to author confidence rather than to examiner-trap density.
findings.recommendation: Sweep Amir, Sam, Marcus, Sarah, Beth in that order to citation-parity with Brennan (11) — each missing pearl/pitfall gets a one-line type:nice / type:bsped / type:rcog citation. Specifically: Amir's corrected-Na warning and cerebral-oedema mortality both need BSPED 2021 §X.Y refs; Sarah's TVUSS-first-line and Anti-D status both need the NG126 §1.4 line.
findings.evidence: Citation tallies: case_paeds_dka_amir.yaml 4 sources, case_anaphylaxis_paeds_sibling.yaml 9, case_ectopic_minors_sarah.yaml 10, case_dka_marcus.yaml 12 (sample) vs Brennan 11, Ahmed 16, Okonkwo 17, Kowalski 18. HANDOVER.md §5 Clinical TODO ('Sam, Amir, Brennan, Oduya, UGIB could deepen' — partially listed but Amir is the worst offender and is missed).

findings.title: Pause-budget and ambient throttling are absent from the kernel — the 'busy ED' pillar is unbuilt
findings.body: The original build prompt opens with 'pressure should feel like a busy ED, not a reaction-time test' and the audit-fixes-3 note (HANDOVER §5) explicitly calls out a 30s/15s-per-shift-minute pause budget. Neither the term pause_budget nor any ambient throttling exists in the codebase (grep returns zero hits). Today the kernel runs at sim-speed-multiplied wall time and the player can pause indefinitely between every interaction; there is no felt cost to dwelling. Conversely, 13 of 17 shifts ship as solo cases (one focus, zero ambient), and only the hen-do shift fields the prompt's stated 'focus + ambient' shape with 4 patients. The 'simulation depth bar' is Dwarf Fortress — DF works because the world ticks whether you watch or not AND the watching itself is expensive. Skitt does the first, not the second. Underlying cause: ambient cases were de-prioritised after M8 once solo shifts unlocked faster authoring; pause-cost was never wired because it required a kernel change and no episode demanded it.
findings.recommendation: Add `kernel.pauseBudget: { used_s: number; cap_s: number }` decrementing during isRunning=false and surfaced on ClockBar as a thin bar. Default cap = 30s per shift-minute. When exhausted, the kernel emits a McGrath 'standing-around' interrupt and ambient case state silently progresses. Re-shape the solo shifts that already have plausible ambient siblings (Williams + Brennan exists as DOAC double-bill but the rest are solo) — at minimum, Marcus + Morrison, Okafor + Patel, Ahmed + Okonkwo are clinically coherent dyads already in the catalogue.
findings.evidence: Bundle-wide grep returns zero for pause_budget/ambient_throttl; src/sim/kernel.ts L1577–1623 (advance/start/pause have no budget concept); HANDOVER.md §5 Gameplay TODOs (both items still open); src/App.tsx L782–903 SHIFT_DEFS (13 of 17 are single-case).

findings.title: No mid-shift fail-state escape — the kernel turns one bad clinical call into a 20-minute punishment
findings.body: When a case transitions to 'deceased' the kernel sets pendingDeathNotice (L2043–2049), the modal fires with 'continue shift' or 'debrief now' (EncounterScreen L3576–3582), and that's the end of the kernel's contribution. There is no path to retry just the failed case while keeping the rest of the shift; replayShift() at App.tsx L964 only restarts the entire episode from T+0. In two-case shifts (hen-do, family, metabolic, DOAC double, safety-net) that means the player has to either swallow ten more minutes of doing nothing while Sam's case is alive or scrap the whole shift and lose Sarah's resus too. This is a fail mode that punishes the curious learner — exactly the audience the project is for. Underlying cause: replay was scoped at episode granularity in M4 and never revisited as the case count grew; the deceased terminal state is a kernel ledger entry, not a UI affordance.
findings.recommendation: Add `kernel.rewindCase(caseId, toTransitionId)` that resets one CaseRuntime to its pre-deceased snapshot (last entered or last stable state — both are already on cs.reasons). Wire a 'rewind this case (study mode)' button beside 'debrief now' in PatientDeathModal, with a flag on the shift's debrief that the case was studied not played. Tier this off in F1 difficulty; leave it on in CT1.
findings.evidence: src/sim/kernel.ts L2042–2049 (death set), L2073 dismissDeathNotice only clears the notice; src/App.tsx L964–973 (replayShift restarts episode); EncounterScreen.tsx L3576–3582 (PatientDeathModal has only continue/debrief). HANDOVER.md §5 Gameplay 'Fail-state escape' TODO names this exactly.

findings.title: Epilogues are sometimes the best writing in the file and sometimes a footnote — inconsistency teaches mistrust
findings.body: Beth's wrong-discharge epilogue ('She is back at 23:40 with biphasic angioedema. Tom rings 999 from the car park.') is exactly the consequence-writing the prompt asks for — a paragraph after the checkbox. Brennan's gets it right with 'Andexanet alfa runs over 30 minutes. Liam is at her bedside. He sits where she can see his face when she wakes up.' But Patel's wrong-thrombolysis epilogue is 'Door-to-balloon would have been 78 minutes from here. The decision is reviewable next week at M&M.' — a procedure note. And Stan's wrong-discharge epilogue threads back to the publican of the Crown in a way the other cases don't. The variance is wider than the audit's stated bar ('the patient's / family's point of view at the next narrative beat' — schema.ts L2568–2571). Underlying cause: epilogues were added as a M56 batch with no second pass; the strongest were written first, the rest filled in to clear the slot.
findings.recommendation: One author-pass on the 17 wrong-disposition epilogues with a single rule: name a person who is not in the bay and what they are doing at that moment. (Beth: Tom in car park. Brennan: Liam at bedside. Stan: publican. Patel: M&M committee — but who, doing what? — fix.) The right-disposition epilogues are mostly fine; the wrong-disposition ones are where the player learns the cost.
findings.evidence: case_anaphylaxis_adult_peanut.yaml L5724 (Beth biphasic); case_head_injury_doac_brennan.yaml L9651 (Brennan PCC); case_chest_pain_patel_ambient.yaml L7681 (M&M); case_intox_stan_ambient.yaml L10842 (publican). Schema definition src/content/schema.ts L2562–2574.
